programme: An IFN-γ–JAK/STAT1 antigen-presentation axis: STAT1 induces IRF1, IRF1 and its dimerization partner/functional counterweight IRF2 co-regulate the MHC class I/II presentation machinery (targets shared by all three include CIITA, TAP2, PSMB9, IFNG, FASLG, NOS2, CDKN1A), and TBX21 (T-bet) sits upstream as the Th1/CD8+ lineage-commitment factor that drives the IFNG production feeding this loop (TBX21 targets include IFNG, CXCR3, ICOS, HAVCR2, CD8A, STAT4).
role_in_a: In lung cancer this axis sets tumor-intrinsic antigen presentation and cytotoxic T-cell infiltration: STAT1 signaling (via C1QBP-STAT1, MHC-I/IGF2 fibroblast crosstalk, and epitranscriptomic control of Th differentiation) and IRF1 (via TRIM21-mediated degradation control, and a miRNA network) shape immune visibility and radio/immuno-resistance in NSCLC, with TBX21-marked T-helper/dendritic responses reported in the tumor immune compartment.
role_in_b: In melanoma the same nodes govern MHC-I-dependent immune escape and checkpoint-blockade response: STAT1 is repeatedly reported to modulate PD-L1/MHC-I expression and progression (via NLRP3, mTORC2, TUBB4A), IRF1 acts through SOX10-linked metastasis and NAD/IFN-γ/PD-L1 crosstalk, and IRF2 loss reduces MHC-I transcripts and drives CD8+ T-cell exhaustion, directly restraining anti-tumor immunity.
shared_axis: Lung cancer and melanoma are the two flagship malignancies managed with IFN-γ/PD-(L)1-axis immunotherapy, and in both, tumor-intrinsic JAK/STAT1 output funneled through IRF1 (presentation) and IRF2 (exhaustion/evasion) — fed by T-bet-driven cytotoxic T-cell IFN-γ output — is the mechanism that determines whether a tumor stays visible to CD8+ T cells or escapes; the same GBP2–STAT1 module is reported to act on PD-L1/ferroptosis biology in each disease separately.
reasoning: STAT1, IRF1, IRF2 and TBX21 are independently placed with disease-specific mechanistic papers in both lung cancer and melanoma, and the module they form (IFN-γ–STAT1–IRF1/IRF2 antigen presentation, with TBX21 as the upstream T-cell driver) is a coherent, textbook-nameable pathway rather than an artifact of the target-overlap counts. No single retrieved paper states 'lung cancer and melanoma share this axis' as a direct comparative claim, but the GBP2-STAT1-PD-L1 mechanism recurring separately in NSCLC (41286130) and melanoma (41444224), plus IRF2's pan-cancer CD8 exhaustion paper (36370712), makes the shared-axis inference follow rather than requiring speculation from anatomy alone.
support: 41286130 (GBP2 regulates lung cancer progression through STAT1/glycolysis), 41444224 (GBP2 condensates and STAT1-linked ferroptosis sensitize melanoma to anti-PD-L1), 40471501 (curcumin reduces STAT1 phosphorylation to block IFN-γ-induced PD-L1 in lung A549 cells), 36370712 (IRF2 drives IFN-mediated CD8+ T-cell exhaustion, pan-cancer including both tissues), 39354629 (IRF2 loss reduces MHC-I pathway transcripts across human cancers including melanoma), 42020516 (IRF1-TRIM21 axis controls anti-tumor immunity via ubiquitin-mediated degradation in lung cancer), 40808260 (SOX10 regulates melanoma metastasis through IRF1-ITGA3/EphA2-FAK), 41716028 (STAT1 accelerates melanoma progression via TUBB4A, tagged as concerning both diseases), 42593864 (tumor NLRP3 promotes immunotherapy resistance in melanoma by inhibiting STAT1/MHC-I), 40283008 (TBX21 among T-cell transcription factors profiled in stereotactic radiotherapy immune modulation, tagged as concerning both diseases).
how_to_falsify: In matched NSCLC and melanoma tumor/PBMC samples, knock down or knock out STAT1, IRF1, IRF2 and TBX21 individually and in combination, then measure surface MHC class I/II (via CIITA, TAP2, PSMB9 transcript and protein) and CD8+ T-cell infiltration/killing under IFN-γ stimulation; if antigen presentation and cytotoxic response are unaffected by this factor set in both tumor types, or if IRF1/IRF2 do not co-occupy the same MHC-I promoters by ChIP in either tissue, the proposed shared axis is wrong.
caveats: Only 1 independent cohort pair underlies the 252 patient-group comparisons, so the high recurrence counts (up to 118/252) reflect stratification within a small number of source cohorts rather than independent replication — treat the concordance as internally consistent, not externally validated. PAX5, PAX4, CRX, ZBTB4, FOXN1, FOXD3, AIRE and PITX2 were deliberately left out of the programme: their retrieved evidence is either single-disease, tangential (e.g., FOXN1 only in lung squamous carcinoma, PAX5 evidence is for Merkel cell carcinoma not melanoma proper), or not mechanistically linked to the STAT1/IRF/TBX21 module, and including them would overstate coherence. None of the excluded single-view or tissue-generic factors were needed to build this account, consistent with the module resting on recurrent, non-tissue-generic factors.
